corrected_answer:
Treat corpus-01515 (scenario variant 215) as an underspecified incident: the accelerator, model, dtype, parallelism, runtime/allocator, memory limit, scheduler, and cache implementation are unknown, so no platform-specific cause or capacity should be assumed. Preserve request IDs and admission, prefill, decode, completion/cancellation, and OOM timestamps.

Prioritize evidence collection. For every matched request and concurrency level, record prompt/generated-token lengths, live sequences, batch/prefill size, cancellations, per-request KV bytes and growth, allocated and reserved device bytes, largest free block and fragmentation, transient workspace and collective buffers, cache residency/retention and cleanup delay, host RSS/pinned/shared memory, and swap. Check max sequence/context and batch limits, active-sequence accounting, admission behavior, and whether paged or prefix caching is truly enabled. Keep measured bytes separate from estimates and use bytes/GiB consistently.

Falsifiable H1: within prespecified prompt/output-length and concurrency strata, live KV plus transient allocations exceed measured usable device headroom immediately before OOM. Support requires the predicted per-request KV slope and headroom crossing to replicate; falsify it if OOM occurs with ample headroom or if the signal disappears after controlling allocator fragmentation/workspace/collective/host memory. Competing hypotheses are fragmentation (reserved minus allocated and largest-free-block collapse), workspace/collective spikes, leaked or retained cache, host exhaustion, or an accounting/scheduler bug.

Run a controlled experiment: freeze versions and model/configuration, replay randomized matched requests across length and concurrency strata with enough repetitions and warm-up, and change one factor at a time (context cap, batch/admission limit, paged/prefix cache, quantization, allocator setting, and cache cleanup) against a baseline. Correlate request-level outcomes with synchronized device/host/KV/allocator/workspace traces. Report OOM, rejection, timeout, and cancellation denominators separately, plus correctness, TTFT/TPOT, throughput, tail latency, and relevant SLOs with uncertainty; do not treat a single successful replay as proof.

Mitigate conservatively and in order: bound context/output and batch/concurrency, reject or queue before predicted headroom is unsafe, clean up cancelled sequences and bound cache retention, then evaluate paged/prefix caching or quantization only with quality/correctness checks. Isolate workspace/collective and host-memory fixes after attribution. Canary changes with fixed rollback gates for OOM/rejection/error rates, correctness, latency, throughput, and host/device headroom; immediately revert on breach. Evidence is required before claiming root cause or generalizing beyond the tested workload.

Check max sequence/context and batch limits, active-sequence accounting, admission behavior, and whether paged or prefix caching is truly enabled. Keep measured bytes separate from estimates and use bytes/GiB consistently.

Falsifiable H1: within prespecified prompt/output-length and concurrency strata, live KV plus transient allocations exceed measured usable device headroom immediately before OOM. Competing hypotheses are fragmentation (reserved minus allocated and largest-free-block collapse), workspace/collective spikes, leaked or retained cache, host exhaustion, or an accounting/scheduler bug.

Run a controlled experiment: freeze versions and model/configuration, replay randomized matched requests across length and concurrency strata with enough repetitions and warm-up, and change one factor at a time (context cap, batch/admission limit, paged/prefix cache, quantization, allocator setting, and cache cleanup) against a baseline. Correlate request-level outcomes with synchronized device/host/KV/allocator/workspace traces. Report OOM, rejection, timeout, and cancellation denominators separately, plus correctness, TTFT/TPOT, throughput, tail latency, and relevant SLOs with uncertainty; do not treat a single successful replay as proof.

Mitigate conservatively and in order: bound context/output and batch/concurrency, reject or queue before predicted headroom is unsafe, clean up cancelled sequences and bound cache retention, then evaluate paged/prefix caching or quantization only with quality/correctness checks. Isolate workspace/collective and host-memory fixes after attribution. Canary changes with fixed rollback gates for OOM/rejection/error rates, correctness, latency, throughput, and host/device headroom; immediately revert on breach. Evidence is required before claiming root cause or generalizing beyond the tested workload.
